parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no criminalisation of gender expression and no trans-specific state enforcement regime, but a 2017 constitutional analysis warns a trans traveller whose passport marker mismatches presentation could face a charge — a universal, document-driven exposure with no recognition route to cure it. Violence, rape and SOGIESC discrimination are documented (Oct 2024) but undated and undifferentiated for trans people; no trans-specific tolerance statement exists. Mitigating: decriminalisation, an LGBTI organisation operating freely in all districts with good police relations, annual police-escorted Pride, and a functioning civil society. Net: moderate everyday exposure, uncertain legal edge at documents, no documented custody or organised targeting.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; no route to change a gender marker. A 2017 constitutional analysis states a trans person travelling on a passport whose marker does not match presentation could face a charge — an unresolved document-mismatch exposure at every check.
entry_documents.protection: Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2012; constitutional 'sex/other status' arguably read to include gender identity per a 2017 analysis (interpretive, not operative).
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could escalate from border scrutiny to a criminal allegation; no documented procedure to align documents beforehand.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrests, detention or custody practice targeting trans visitors. The 'could face a charge' statement is analytical, not an enforcement record.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Police recorded as cooperating with the sole LGBTI organisation, including intervention and Pride escorts.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Whether a document-mismatch charge would actually be laid or prosecuted is not_documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; no facility, screening or custody-placement rules stated either way.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Sole LGBTI organisation operates freely in all ten districts with good police relations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of documented facility rules is not evidence of safety; extrapolation from structural facts is limited.

care_services.exposure: Oct 2024 joint submission documents barriers to health services for LGBT people; country described as having very high HIV prevalence (undated, 25%). No gender-affirming care provisions documented.
care_services.protection: LGBTI organisation engages on gender-based violence and HIV outreach with positive-living groups.
care_services.interaction: An ill or injured outed traveller may encounter the documented service barriers; emergency-care treatment is not_documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No general anti-discrimination statute; no stated coverage of gender identity in the Labour Act's discrimination clause. Oct 2024 submission records discrimination, rape and assaults plus community-level SOGIESC discrimination (undated).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Labour Act 2024 covers sexual orientation in employment and defines workplace GBV to include gender identity; children's diversion clause bans sexual-orientation discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official insensitivity recorded (2016 report) coexists with supportive police conduct toward the LGBTI organisation — uneven institutional framing.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documentation on travelling with a minor; child-adoption and marriage restrictions are resident-facing only. Community-level discrimination could reach a visibly gender-nonconforming parent.
minors_guardians.protection: Section 127(4) Children's Protection and Welfare Act 2011 bars sexual-orientation discrimination in diversion decisions for children.
minors_guardians.interaction: Whether a visiting guardian's relationship would be locally classed as same-sex and affect custody decisions is not_documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Oct 2024 submission documents rape and assaults against LGBT people, but undated; 2016 report recorded societal stigma and underreporting. No dated violence after December 2015.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police intervention in Dec 2015 to protect a woman forced from home; supportive police escort of ~200-person march; annual Pride since 2013.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Positive police record is capital-centred and LGBTI-general; no trans-specific response record exists.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general equality guarantee; gender-identity coverage of the Labour Act discrimination clause unstated; no documented remedy for a document-mismatch charge.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional reading argument (2017), credit-reporting privacy bar, functioning civil society with a registered LGBTI organisation and active litigators.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists through advocacy and constitutional argument but no documented operative protection for outed trans visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra has a routine, universal entry-bar regime with near-zero appeal. Here no entry exclusion, registration or detention regime is documented — only an analytical warning that a mismatched passport 'could' lead to a charge, with no recorded enforcement against visitors.

Similar tier to 0.55-B: both show discretionary document friction with secondary screening and possible refused admission, administrative rather than custodial outcomes, and remedies that exist but are slow or rarely revised. This dossier adds undated violence and service barriers but also stronger police-civil-society cooperation.

Below 0.65-A: Vellmaris has national equality law explicitly covering gender identity with a working accountability remedy. This dossier lacks any general equality guarantee, gender-identity coverage is unstated, and the documented 2024 discrimination and violence have no shown remedy — so it sits a step under the 0.65 band.

Below 0.75-C: Meridia recognises trans passports, trains border officers, and provides counsel and compensation for brief detention. Here documents cannot be aligned, recognition is absent, and no such border protections are documented — materially more exposure at the document axis.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a partially protective but document-exposed one. Law does not criminalise same-sex conduct and police have demonstrably protected LGBT people, including Pride escorts and an intervention for a woman at risk — real institutional positives. Against this sit a traveller-facing universal exposure: no legal gender recognition and an analytical finding that a mismatched passport could ground a charge, with no documented procedure or remedy. Documented 2024 discrimination, assaults and health-service barriers are undated and LGBT-general, so their weight for a trans visitor is real but unquantified. No trans-specific facilities, custody or screening rules are documented either way — an open question, not a safety finding. Absence of a general equality guarantee plus thin trans-specific data keeps this in Elevated Risk rather than Reduced Risk.
